headline: Town boards prepared for the March 2 Special Town Meeting on Neary School renovations, while advancing FY27 municipal and regional school budgets and hiking water rates.
synopsis: In February 2026, Southborough officials focused on preparations for the March 2 Special Town Meeting, which features four articles addressing Neary School renovation studies, campus consolidation, and roof borrowing. The Advisory Committee recommended a preliminary $70.9 million FY27 municipal operating budget, while the Select Board debated staffing costs and approved a 9 percent volumetric water rate increase. The Regional School Committee approved a $31.4 million FY27 operating budget for Algonquin, applying $675,000 from reserves to offset rising costs. Meanwhile, the Planning Board voted to withdraw a proposed 55-plus housing bylaw from the spring Town Meeting warrant following resident feedback. Regional school officials also reconsidered and approved the 2026-2027 academic calendar.

top_items.title: School feasibility and roof articles for Special Town Meeting
top_items.why: School officials and town boards aligned positions on four March 2 Special Town Meeting articles addressing Neary School renovations, alternate campus consolidations, and roof borrowing.
top_items.body: Article 1 seeks up to $175,000 from free cash to fund a feasibility study and schematic design for renovating Neary School, backed by the School Committee, Select Board, and Advisory Committee. Articles 2 and 3 request $500,000 and $324,000 to study expanding Trottier and Finn to decommission Neary; school leaders recommend defeating both, noting grade reconfigurations would require additions of up to 12,000 square feet. Article 4 seeks borrowing of up to $6.85 million to replace Neary's failing roof and fund accessibility upgrades, though ADA costs would roll into Article 1 if approved, lowering roof borrowing to $4.5 million.

top_items.title: Advisory Committee recommends preliminary $70.9 million FY27 budget
top_items.why: The Advisory Committee voted 6-0 to recommend a $70,887,098 preliminary FY27 operating budget to Town Meeting and the Select Board.
top_items.body: The committee agreed that municipal departments held operational costs to level service, leaving capital articles and bond authorizations as remaining adjustments. Under current assumptions, single-family taxes are estimated to rise about 5.3 percent, and the budget balances within the levy limit with roughly $91,000 to spare. Select Board members later reviewed the figures, debating whether to preserve two recently added police patrol officer positions or institute an immediate hiring freeze.

top_items.title: Regional School Committee approves $31.4 million FY27 budget
top_items.why: The Regional School Committee voted 6-0 to approve a $31,416,287 operating budget for FY27, representing a 5.81 percent increase over FY26.
top_items.body: Over 59 percent of the regional budget increase is driven by out-of-district special education tuitions, special education transportation, and a 9.99 percent rise in health insurance costs. To reduce assessments to Southborough and Northborough, the committee voted unanimously to apply $675,000 from Excess and Deficiency reserves and approved a $477,000 capital assessment. The budget now heads to upcoming Town Meetings in both member towns.

top_items.title: Select Board approves water rate increase for FY27
top_items.why: The Select Board voted unanimously to increase FY27 water base charges by 12.6 percent and volumetric rates by 9.0 percent across all four tiers.
top_items.body: The rate hikes were recommended following an FY27 Water Rate Study presented by Department of Public Works officials and consultants. The rate increase is designed to support the water enterprise fund, cover rising capital expenses, and make progress toward a 20 percent retained earnings target.

top_items.title: Planning Board withdraws 55-plus housing bylaw from warrant
top_items.why: The Planning Board voted 5-0 to withdraw a proposed 55-plus housing zoning bylaw from the April 2026 Annual Town Meeting warrant.
top_items.body: The proposal sought to amend the town's zoning bylaw concerning age-qualified housing developments. Board members and housing advocates agreed that substantial resident feedback warranted deeper study before presenting changes to voters, voting unanimously to pull the article and close the public hearing.

top_items.title: Regional School Committee adopts Option 5 academic calendar
top_items.why: The Regional School Committee voted 4-1-1 on reconsideration to approve calendar Option 5 for the 2026-2027 school year.
top_items.body: The revised calendar aligns Algonquin Regional High School's operations with member towns by removing staff professional development days from Yom Kippur and Eid and scheduling a professional development day on Orthodox Good Friday. The vote reconsidered the committee's earlier calendar decision from December 2025.

top_items.title: Industrial Park zoning overhaul advances toward Town Meeting
top_items.why: The Planning Board held a public hearing on a major overhaul of Industrial Park district regulations before continuing the hearing to March 9.
top_items.body: The proposed zoning amendment updates allowed uses across the Industrial Park district, creates town performance standards for noise and emissions, and establishes regulations governing data centers and battery energy storage systems ahead of Annual Town Meeting.
